title: Cylindrical base
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In this sketch, draw a first loop consisting of a circle centered at coordinates (0.0083, 0.0083) with a radius of 0.0083. Add a second loop by drawing another circle with the same center but a smaller radius of 0.0068. After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.0165 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it using the same vector as before. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction to create a cylindrical base. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction, resulting in a new solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical base are a length of 0.016544117647058824 units, a width of 0.016544117647058824 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the cylindrical section
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0083, 0.0083)  # Move to the center of the circles
    .circle(0.0083)         # Outer circle
    .circle(0.0068)         # Inner circle
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylindrical section
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Create the small rectangular section at the top
rect = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0083, 0.0083)  # Move to the center of the rectangle
    .rect(0.0165, 0.0165)    # Create a square with side length 0.0165
    .extrude(0.01)           # Extrude the rectangle by a small height
)

# Combine the cylindrical section and the rectangular section
r = cylinder.union(rect)
